memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"In your unfailing love you will lead the people you have redeemed. In your
strength you will guide them to your holy dwelling." - Ex 15:13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The song turns from what God has done to what He will do. And the verbs are
gentle: lead, guide.

Notice the order in this verse. He redeemed them first, then He leads them. That
order never changes in Scripture. God does not lead people toward redemption on
condition of good behaviour; He redeems, and then He leads the redeemed.

Notice also the destination: "your holy dwelling." The exodus was never only
about getting out of Egypt. It was about getting to God. Deliverance from was
always in service of deliverance to.

That is easy to lose. We can be so focused on escaping something, a habit, a
situation, a season, that we forget salvation is fundamentally about being
brought near to God. Peter writes that "Christ also suffered once for sins, the
righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God" (1 Pet 3:18). That last
phrase is the point of the whole sentence.

And the fuel for the journey is "unfailing love." The Hebrew word here speaks of
covenant loyalty, love that has committed itself and will not walk away. God does
not lead us out of duty. He leads us out of a love that has bound itself to us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you more focused on what you are escaping or on the God you are heading
   toward?
2. Do you believe God's love toward you is committed, not conditional?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that You redeemed me and now lead me. Bring me nearer to
Yourself, and let me rest in Your unfailing love. Amen.
